title: Profiles of Motorists Caught for Speeding Violations and Adapting Education Programmes and Penalties to Those at Higher Risk of Offending
what_it_is: Profiles of Motorists Caught for Speeding Violations and Adapting Education Programmes and Penalties to Those at Higher Risk of Offending

sections.label: Speeding offender data 2024
sections.summary: Speeding offenders in 2024 were disproportionately males, Singapore Citizens and car drivers; Traffic Police does not track driving experience.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs): Sir, based on the data on speeding violations in 2024, males, Singapore Citizens and those driving cars are disproportionately represented amongst speeding offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: The Traffic Police (TP) does not track the data based on years of driving experience.

sections.label: Penalties for repeat speeding offenders
sections.summary: Recalcitrant or multiple offenders face higher penalties, with the Road Traffic Act mandating licence suspension and minimum sentences for some repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: As for the penalty framework, those who commit multiple offences or are recalcitrant offenders can expect to receive higher penalties.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: In addition, the Road Traffic Act mandates heavier penalties, such as suspension of licence and mandatory minimum sentences for certain profiles of repeat offenders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: TP does not track the reasons for speeding.

sections.label: Alcohol driving penalties and limits review
sections.summary: Penalties were increased in 2019 with mandatory imprisonment and disqualification for alcohol-influenced dangerous driving, and alcohol concentration limits are being reviewed.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: To tackle this, we increased our penalties in 2019 with mandatory imprisonment and mandatory disqualification of licence for dangerous and careless driving offences, if the offenders were under the influence of alcohol.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: In addition, we are reviewing the maximum allowable breath and blood alcohol concentration limits and will announce the details when ready.

sections.label: Speed enforcement and red-light cameras
sections.summary: Speed enforcement will be activated on more red-light cameras in 2025 and more enforcement work will be done on the ground.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, we are pleased that people are more cognisant of the fact that they need to be careful, they need to make sure that they practise road safety habits and so forth.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: So, with this in mind, we will also continue to activate the speed enforcement function on more red-light cameras in 2025 and at the same time, we will also do more enforcement work on the ground.
